the-secret-lifecycle-inventory-ownership.r: A cloud access key was found in a public repository and nobody knew which systems used it. The key was over four years old, had broad permissions and had no recorded owner.
the-secret-lifecycle-inventory-ownership.x: Most incidents come from old secrets that nobody owns, so lifecycle thinking turns strings into managed assets.

finding-and-stopping-leaks-in-code-ci-an.r: A token for the package registry appeared in a public build log after a debug flag was turned on. A developer had enabled verbose output while debugging, and the tool printed its configuration, including the token.
finding-and-stopping-leaks-in-code-ci-an.x: A secret in history stays there, so prevention and a calm response both matter. Practise it on a scratch environment first.

delivering-secrets-to-kubernetes-workloa.r: A database password was rotated and the application kept failing until every pod was restarted. The operator refreshed the Secret on time, but the application read the password from an environment variable at start, so running pods kept the old value and failed after the old password was revoked.
delivering-secrets-to-kubernetes-workloa.x: A Kubernetes Secret is encoded, not encrypted by default, and running pods may not see a rotated value.

certificate-inventory-expiry-monitoring-.r: A partner integration failed at night because a certificate on an old gateway expired. The gateway was set up three years earlier by a team that had since moved, and its certificate was renewed by hand each year.
certificate-inventory-expiry-monitoring-.x: Expiry is known months ahead, so outages happen only when the certificate is forgotten. Practise it on a scratch environment first.

operating-cert-manager-issuers-acme-and-.r: A new service had no certificate after the deployment and the ingress served a default one. The ingress rule for the service forced a redirect and a rewrite that sent the challenge path to the application, which returned 404.
operating-cert-manager-issuers-acme-and-.x: Know the objects and their events and most failures explain themselves. Practise it on a scratch environment first.

workload-identity-spiffe-and-key-managem.r: A federation trust accepted tokens from any repository in the organisation. The role trusted every repository in the organisation, so a test repository with weak review could obtain production deploy rights.
workload-identity-spiffe-and-key-managem.x: The safest secret is the one that never exists, so short lived tokens beat stored passwords. Practise it on a scratch environment first.
